answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, externally earned resource before it can claim rewards or vote; the protocol caps influence by bonded stake, not by the number of identities. If a sable account or an umber account is caught double-claiming, verifiable logs trigger slashing, so splitting one operator across many names does not multiply influence. A quill attacker must lock more real value for every extra identity and risks losing it, making a Sybil campaign costly rather than free.
